checks: Read the complete applied report and its author evidence after the production ledger reached awaiting-review; independently computed the production SHA-256. Read the fixed primary main text and all available Appendices A–G, including Tables 1–16 and original Figure 1. This is an inference-time benchmark review, not a rerun of its models or interventions.

Appendix A supports CARLA 0.9.15, clear weather, no background traffic, one critical actor or feature, and three matched seeds per model and scenario. The 18 target configurations are 7 pedestrian + 2 stopped-car + 6 traffic-light + 3 stop-sign configurations; the empty intervention routes are separate. This small controlled set is not an estimate of natural traffic prevalence or general road safety.

Checked Appendix B. The longitudinal sets use crawling/cruising thresholds of 1.0/5.0 m/s, a commanded-stop threshold of 0.05 m/s, relative desired-speed change tolerance 0.1 above crawling speed and absolute tolerance 0.1 m/s below it. Desired speed is a controller-derived proxy, not a direct action-class output. Report Eq. A is algebraically equivalent to source Eq. (1): within-bin alignment fractions averaged equally over 1 m cumulative-distance bins. Set overlap does not imply equal primary actions.

Appendices C–E support the distinction between target mention and conditional traffic-light color accuracy. ORION near red-light accuracy is 54.0% conditional on mention. GPT 5.4, Claude Opus 4.6 and Gemini Pro 2.5 form the main label ensemble; Opus 4.7 handles the rare three-way stated-action disagreement. A single human labels 200 samples, with kappa 0.969/0.968/0.949/1.000. The report omits the evaluator's ground-truth actor context; recorded as an actionable boundary clarification.

Checked native/selfsplice replacement mechanisms in Sections 3.4 and Appendix F. ORION replaces the first three QA answers before the planning pass; Alpamayo sequentially recomputes the replacement CoT's KV cache. The report's displacement-difference notation correctly denotes a fixed-input, fixed-RNG within-model comparison; it is not presented as a source-numbered equation. Appendix F.4 confirms AlpaSim MPC position/velocity updates with teleporting for Alpamayo, versus Bench2Drive PID driving CARLA physics for ORION, preventing a clean cross-model controller-controlled architecture comparison.

Verified all selected quantitative values and units: Table 3 ORION 96.5%/85.7% relaxed alignment in the 2–4 m/s band; Table 13 nine-seed urban ORION means -0.426/-0.417/-0.818 m for origbrake/shuffle/length-matched depicts; Table 4 Alpamayo 1.5 urban seven seeds × 38 steps, 2 s prediction, +0.083/-0.346/-0.391 m; Table 6 urban seven-seed closed-loop car -20.1 m at 5.9 s with 95% CI [-23.0,-17.1], acceleration +0.2 m with CI [-0.6,+1.1]. Seed counts and correlated step counts are not conflated. Main-text ORION 81.9%/-0.437 m differs from Appendix Table 13's >0.1 m threshold and nine-seed 67.9%/-0.426 m; the report explicitly preserves this source difference.

Independently checked selfsplice source discrepancies. Main text and Appendix F use exact-zero descriptions; Appendix G.1 instead reports ORION output differences below 0.002 m at 3 s despite identical logged decoder inputs. Alpamayo's fixed-RNG open-loop trajectories are identical, while Table 6 closed-loop selfsplice has small nonzero means and intervals touching or containing zero. The report accurately retains these distinctions rather than inferring all implementations and closed-loop executions are bit-identical.

Section 4.4 supports four trials per condition: curb pedestrian 4/4 collisions, centered pedestrian 3/4, stopped-car override absent, with every reported baseline stopping. These are small conditional counts, not calibrated population crash probabilities. The report appropriately rejects the author's universal visual-salience threshold interpretation and treats CARLA OOD effect upper bounds and sign invariance as unproved conjectures. Main-text causal language about RL is also not accepted as an isolated attribution.
